topic:
Managing Screen Time Wisely  
Useful expressions: "digital detox," "set boundaries," "track usage."
script: Hey everyone, welcome to "Chillwave B2".
I'm Ethan.
Tonight, I want to talk about something we all struggle with—managing screen time wisely.
I caught myself scrolling through my phone for an hour last night without even realizing it.
Let’s take it easy and chat about how to track usage, set boundaries, and maybe even try a digital detox.

Heh, I used to scroll my phone mindlessly until 2 a.m. every night. Last week, I finally checked the "track usage" stats and realized I was on my phone four hours daily. I started setting boundaries, like no screens during dinner or right before bed. My weekends now include a "digital detox" — just reading or walking without my phone. Honestly, it’s weird how much calmer I feel now. Do you ever notice how late you stay on your devices?
Heh, I had a friend tell me she unplugged her TV for a week and just… stared at the wall.
Turns out, she rediscovered her old sketchbook and started drawing again.
It’s kind of funny how taking a break can lead you to other stuff you forgot you liked.
I’ve been trying to avoid checking my email first thing in the morning, too.
It’s way better to drink coffee and listen to some tunes for a bit instead.
Have you ever gone a full day without scrolling your phone?
Heh, I’ve started keeping my phone in another room after 9 p.m. — it’s surprising how quickly bedtime becomes actual sleep when you’re not doomscrolling.
Sometimes I’ll grab a book or just sit in the dark and think about nothing, which feels weird at first but kinda nice.
I’m curious — what’s one thing you’ve done lately that didn’t involve a screen?
Maybe it was cooking, or chatting with a friend, or just… existing for a bit.
Those little moments add up, and honestly, they’re way better than mindlessly tapping on a screen.
So, what’s something you’ve missed lately that you might try bringing back?

Alright, for a quick tip tonight—have you heard of "screen-free zones"? It’s just a nice way to say areas where you keep devices out, like your bedroom or the dinner table. I’ve made my bathroom a screen-free zone, and it’s helped me unwind better. Yeah, no emails or news while brushing your teeth—sounds silly, but it works! You could try making one part of your day a "screen-free moment" to give your mind a break.
So, maybe tonight’s takeaway is this: a little less scrolling can make room for a lot more living.
Thanks for sticking around and chatting about all this — it’s always good to have someone else thinking about the same stuff.
If you try one small thing this week, let me know how it goes.
Night, everyone. Stay offline sometimes, and I’ll be here next time.
